betaNB: Bootstrap for Regression Effect Sizes

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

2026-11-28 04:24:44

Source: vignettes/betaNB.Rmd
betaNB.Rmd

Description

Generates nonparametric bootstrap confidence intervals (Efron and Tibshirani, 1993, doi:10.1201/9780429246593) for standardized regression coefficients (beta) and other effect sizes, including multiple correlation, semipartial correlations, squared semipartial correlations, improvement in R-squared, squared partial correlations, Cohen’s f-squared, and differences in standardized regression coefficients, for models fitted by lm(). Pairs and wild bootstrap samples are supported, with percentile, bias-corrected, bias-corrected and accelerated, and modified percentile intervals.

Installation

You can install the CRAN release of betaNB with:

install.packages("betaNB")

You can install the development version of betaNB from GitHub with:

if (!require("pak")) install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("jeksterslab/betaNB")

Example

In this example, a multiple regression model is fitted using program quality ratings (QUALITY) as the regressand/outcome variable and number of published articles attributed to the program faculty members (NARTIC), percent of faculty members holding research grants (PCTGRT), and percentage of program graduates who received support (PCTSUPP) as regressor/predictor variables using a data set from 1982 ratings of 46 doctoral programs in psychology in the USA (National Research Council, 1982). Confidence intervals for the standardized regression coefficients are generated using the BetaNB() function from the betaNB package following Efron & Tibshirani (1993).

library(package = betaNB)
df <- betaNB::nas1982

Fit the regression model using the lm() function. 

object <- stats::lm(formula = QUALITY ~ NARTIC + PCTGRT + PCTSUPP, data = df)

Generate the sampling distribution using nonparametric bootstrapping. 

nb <- NB(object = object, R = 5000L, seed = 0508)

Estimate the standardized regression slopes and the corresponding confidence intervals. 

BetaNB(object = nb, alpha = 0.05)
#> Call:
#> BetaNB(object = nb, alpha = 0.05)
#> 
#> Standardized regression slopes
#> type = "pc"
#>            est     se    R   2.5%  97.5%
#> NARTIC  0.4951 0.0718 5000 0.3567 0.6369
#> PCTGRT  0.3915 0.0766 5000 0.2349 0.5340
#> PCTSUPP 0.2632 0.0786 5000 0.1064 0.4135

Other Features

The package provides the following functions.

Function Purpose
NB() Nonparametric bootstrap (pairs or wild) of a fitted lm model
BetaNB() Standardized regression coefficients
RSqNB() R-squared and adjusted R-squared
DiffBetaNB() Differences of standardized regression coefficients
SCorNB() Semipartial correlations
SCorSqNB() Squared semipartial correlations (squared signed interval)
PCorNB() Squared partial correlations
DeltaRSqNB() Improvement in R-squared (adjusted differences and modified percentile intervals available)
FSqNB() Cohen’s f-squared and local f-squared

The coef(), vcov(), confint(), summary(), and print() methods are available for the returned objects. Percentile, bias-corrected, and bias-corrected and accelerated intervals are available through the type argument of summary() and confint(). Examples for each function are in the package vignettes.

Effect Sizes

The definitions, formulas, and notes on the intervals are in the help pages of the functions and in the vignette betaNB: Example Using the SCorSqNB and FSqNB Functions.
